units.summary: ParseQuantity now calls CacheString on the Quantity it builds in the int64 fast path and the inf.Dec path, so the canonical string is stored at parse time. This moves the string computation (and its allocation) into every parse and relies on String no longer caching.
units.headline: ParseQuantity now eagerly caches the canonical string
units.reason: Changes what every parsed Quantity holds (q.s) and shifts cost and caching semantics for a widely used public parser.
focus: every return path of ParseQuantity sets s (including the fast path that reuses the input string)
extra allocation cost on parse-heavy paths
callers or tests comparing Quantity with reflect.DeepEqual

units.summary: String no longer writes the computed string back into the receiver; it returns the cached value if present or recomputes it each call. This removes a data race on concurrent String calls but makes String on non-parsed Quantities recompute every time.
units.headline: Quantity.String no longer mutates receiver or caches result
units.reason: Alters caching and mutation semantics of a core method used in encoding, with performance and concurrency consequences.
risk_signals: performance regression for quantities built without ParseQuantity
focus: hot callers that build Quantity via NewQuantity/MustParse alternatives and call String repeatedly
code relying on String populating q.s (DeepEqual comparisons)
encoding paths (JSON, proto) that call String more than once

units.summary: Adds a new exported method that computes the canonical string and always stores it in the receiver. It is meant for callers who own the instance, and is used by ParseQuantity.
units.headline: Add exported Quantity.CacheString that stores canonical string
units.reason: New public API that mutates the receiver and is on the ParseQuantity path.
focus: unconditional write to q.s is a race if called on a shared instance
stale q.s is returned unchanged if a quantity was mutated without clearing s

units.summary: The test now expects ParseQuantity to have set the cached string, instead of expecting it empty after parse and set by String. The expectation was changed to match the new behavior.
units.headline: TestQuantityString now expects string cached at parse time
units.reason: An expectation was changed to match new behavior and an assertion was removed, which could hide a regression.
risk_signals: expectation changed to match new behavior
focus: that the removed check (String populates q.s) is intentionally dropped
that the new assertion q.s == item.expect covers all table entries

units.summary: New test checking that CacheString returns and stores the canonical string, is idempotent, and handles nil. Only adds coverage.
units.headline: Add test for Quantity.CacheString
units.reason: New test only; cannot affect production behavior.

units.summary: Benchmark rewritten to use sub-benchmarks per quantity with b.Loop, and the Precalc variant was removed. Benchmark-only change.
units.headline: Rewrite String benchmark as per-case sub-benchmarks

units.summary: Benchmark rewritten into sub-benchmarks using b.Loop. Benchmark-only change.
units.headline: Rewrite BinarySI String benchmark as sub-benchmarks

units.summary: Benchmark now iterates the shared test cases as sub-benchmarks and ignores the parse result. Benchmark-only change.
units.headline: ParseQuantity benchmark now runs per test case
